card.name: Total amount in parentheses after volume
card.fires_on: The unit or opening bracket right after a quantity, when a parenthesis gives the total amount (mg, mcg, Units) that matches a stated volume or tablet count. Also a word just before 'cost' in price questions.

modes.label: Unit inside total-dose parentheses
modes.description: The unit letters of a total amount given in brackets after a volume, such as mL.
modes.example: Direct administration of less than 0.3 mL (180 mc<<g>>) using ZARXIO prefilled

modes.label: Bracket opening a total
modes.description: An opening bracket after a tablet count that introduces the combined mg amount.
modes.example: Release 750 mg (750 mg) once daily, or two Naproxen Sodium Controlled-Release 500 mg tablets<< (>>1,000 mg) once

modes.label: Price question
modes.description: A word just before 'cost' when asking how much something costs.
modes.example: Have your children help you figure out how much two pounds of carrots<< might>> cost, and other related tasks.

card.writes: It pushes toward words about an amount, an exact figure or a cost, and away from 'each' and per-person words.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a total amount is stated, such as the full dose in mg that matches a volume.
